findings.summary: The three with-iron curves are drawn in the order midplane, Fb plane, Fh plane, so the last-drawn teal trace covers the other two wherever they agree. Measured on the rendered PNG, outside the legend sample the blue and orange traces carry ink only in columns 74 to 133 of the 691 px plot area, about 9 percent of the width; across the remaining 91 percent the reader sees one teal curve under a three-entry legend. The coincidence is the physics the section reports (iron share -96.5, -96.8 and -97.1 percent at +1 m), not a plotting fault, but the picture does not let a reader tell agreement from absence for the two hidden planes. A panel note stating that the planes coincide in the far field, or a dash or lightness separation, would let a reader tell the two apart.

The same three-entry plane legend is drawn twice on one figure, here in the upper panel and again in the middle panel at line 113, and never in the lower panel, although the colours name the same three planes in every panel. One figure-level legend would carry the information once; the second copy spends ink and is what placed a legend over the plateau at the previous head.

The lower panel's y-axis label names the air-core field as (bars), but those marks are drawn with the horizontal-dash marker underscore at line 127 and render as short grey dashes and small squares, not as bars. A reader who wants the air-core value looks for a mark that is not there and may read the dashes as a third series; the label should name the marks as drawn, or the marks should become bars.

The x axis is linear across the whole plotted range of about 11 m, so the near-edge structure that the figure exists to show is compressed into a sliver: the peak at about 0.4 m and the fall by 0.5 m occupy roughly 50 px of the 691 px plot width in the upper panel, and the annotated +6787 percent spike occupies about 14 px in the middle panel. A reader can see that a spike exists but cannot read its shape, and the three planes' near-edge separation is the only place the upper panel shows a difference between them.

All three air-core traces are drawn in one grey with the label _air, so no legend entry or label distinguishes them, while the inline note says only dashed grey air-core. The three strands are visibly separate near the edge, where the prose table puts them at 7.2, 8.2 and 9.2 mT at +1 m, about 8 px apart on this axis, so a reader sees three dashes and cannot say which plane each belongs to. This is the only place in the upper panel where a plane difference is visible at all, which makes the missing attribution costly rather than cosmetic.
